# Derive: full reference for LLMs

> Publish AI-built artifacts (HTML pages, Markdown docs, and slide decks) with a permanent URL, version history, and comments anchored to exact text.

Derive is a workspace for work made with agents. Publish to a lasting URL, keep each revision,
comment on exact text with W3C TextQuoteSelector, edit directly, and control who can read or
change the work. Review rounds are there when a decision needs a named look: the reviewer
answers in comments and sends the work back with a note.

Fair Source and self-hostable (Docker, Fly.io, Railway, Render, Cloudflare Workers). Hosted tier at derive.to. The FSL license converts each release to Apache-2.0 after two years.

---

## Artifact types

| Type | File | Renders as |
|---|---|---|
| Markdown | .md | Rendered prose: headings, lists, tables, fenced code, task lists, GFM |
| HTML | .html | The page itself, sandboxed in an opaque origin with CSP: sandbox |
| HTML deck | .html | Navigable slide deck with nav bar and present mode |

### HTML deck protocol

Slides are `<section class="slide">` elements. Derive detects the protocol and wires up the nav bar automatically. The deck and host communicate via postMessage:

```js
// Deck -> host: report current position
parent.postMessage({ source: 'derive-deck', type: 'state', i: 0, total: 8 }, '*')

// Host -> deck: navigate
parent.postMessage({ source: 'derive-host', type: 'deck', action: 'next' }, '*')
parent.postMessage({ source: 'derive-host', type: 'deck', action: 'prev' }, '*')
parent.postMessage({ source: 'derive-host', type: 'deck', action: 'goto', n: 2 }, '*')
```

### Anchor client protocol

Derive injects `/raw/derive-client.js` into every served artifact. It handles text selection -> comment composer and scroll-to-anchor. It communicates with the host via postMessage:

```js
// Client -> host: user selected text
{ source: 'derive', type: 'selection', text, anchor: { exact, prefix, suffix } }

// Host -> client: scroll to anchor
{ source: 'derive-host', type: 'focus-anchor', anchor: { exact, prefix, suffix }, bias: 0.28 }

// Host -> client: highlight anchor
{ source: 'derive-host', type: 'mark-anchor', id, anchor, active }
```

---

## REST API

Base URL: `https://derive.to` (the reference deployment) or your instance's own origin.
Auth: `Authorization: Bearer $DERIVE_TOKEN` for write operations. Artifacts whose link
role grants viewer or better are readable without auth.

If this file and the live API disagree, trust the live API. Fetched copies go stale.
The current capability surface is at `/.well-known/agent.json`, the agent skill at
`/skill.md`, and the full spec at `/openapi.json` (reference UI at `/docs`).
Human documentation is at `https://docs.derive.to/`; official live artifact examples and their source are
at `/examples`.

### Publish an anonymous draft (no account)

```
POST /v1/drafts
Content-Type: multipart/form-data

file    required  One .html/.md file, or a .zip site (index.html at the root)
title   optional  Display title
```

No Authorization header. Response:

```json
{
  "short_id":  "t8mnac05",
  "draft_url":  "https://t8mnac05.derive.page/",
  "claim_url":  "https://derive.to/claim/<token>",
  "expires_at": "2026-07-28T03:23:03.539Z"
}
```

The draft is live immediately on its own origin, view-by-link only (unlisted,
noindex, never cached), and expires in 72 hours unless claimed. Report the draft
URL, the expiry, and the claim URL to the user. The claim link is the only handle
on an unclaimed draft. Client-supplied access fields are ignored on this route, and
drafts cannot be revised: mint a new draft to iterate, or claim first.

Claiming (a human flow, not an agent one): opening `claim_url` signs the user in
and moves the draft into their workspace as a normal versioned artifact; the draft
URL then 302s to the permanent artifact URL. Related endpoints:

```
GET  /v1/drafts/claim/:token   public: what this claim link is for (title, expiry, draft_url)
POST /v1/drafts/claim          authed: {token} → claims into the caller's active workspace
```

Rate-limited tightly per IP; the general publish limits apply underneath.

### Publish a new artifact

```
POST /v1/artifacts
Content-Type: multipart/form-data

file         required  File blob (name determines type: .md or .html)
title        optional  Display title (defaults to filename)
slug         optional  URL slug
message      optional  Version message
workspace_access  optional  none | member. Sets workspace-member access at their seat role
link_role         optional  none | viewer | commenter | editor. Sets access for anyone holding the URL
listed            optional  none | workspace | public. Sets where the artifact appears for discovery
password          optional  Locks the world link (only meaningful with link_role != none)
visibility        optional  LEGACY public | link | org | password. Still accepted and mapped to the fields above
spa               optional  true/1 for single-page apps (disables sandbox)

Omitted access fields use the workspace default; the factory default is the "team
draft": workspace_access=member, link_role=none, listed=none. Two invariants are
rejected, not coerced: listed=workspace requires workspace_access=member, and
listed=public requires link_role != none.
```

Response:

```json
{
  "short_id": "nk0dsral",
  "url": "https://derive.to/artifacts/my-page-nk0dsral",
  "title": "My page",
  "kind": "file",
  "current_version": 1,
  "versions": [{ "n": 1, "created_at": "...", "message": null }]
}
```

### Publish a new version

```
POST /v1/artifacts/:short_id/versions
Content-Type: multipart/form-data

file       required  New content
message    optional  Version message
resolves   optional  Comma-separated comment IDs to close as part of this publish
```

### Read artifact metadata

```
GET /v1/artifacts/:short_id
```

Returns full metadata: title, kind, workspace_access, link_role, listed, current_version, versions array, tags, my_role.

### Read artifact source

```
GET /v1/artifacts/:short_id/content
GET /v1/artifacts/:short_id/content?v=2
```

Returns raw source. Headers include `X-Derive-Version` and `X-Derive-Kind`.

### Read a share URL as markdown (no token needed)

```
GET /artifacts/<ref>.md
GET /artifacts/<ref>@v2.md
GET /artifacts/<ref>            with header  Accept: text/markdown
```

The share URL's markdown projection (HTML artifacts are converted; a bundle serves its
entry page). Anonymous access works whenever the link itself is viewable (a
password-locked link must be unlocked on the web page first); a pinned version other
than the current one needs a signed-in reader unless the artifact enables public
history. Without the suffix or header the URL serves the web app's HTML shell, whose
content loads client-side.

### Version diff

```
GET /v1/artifacts/:short_id/diff?from=1&to=2
```

Returns line-level diff operations: `{ op: "add" | "del" | "ctx", text }[]`.

### Restore a past version

```
POST /v1/artifacts/:short_id/restore
Content-Type: application/json

{ "version": 1 }
```

Creates a new version pointing to the old blob. History is never rewritten.

### Comments

```
GET  /v1/artifacts/:short_id/comments            list threads (state: open | resolved)
POST /v1/artifacts/:short_id/comments            new thread
POST /v1/artifacts/:short_id/comments/:id/reply  reply in thread
POST /v1/artifacts/:short_id/comments/:id/resolve toggle thread state
```

New thread body:
```json
{
  "body_md": "This section is unclear.",
  "quote": "exact text from the artifact to anchor the comment"
}
```

### Permanent artifact URL

```
GET /raw/:short_id/v/:n/index.html
```

Immutable, cacheable, served with `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox`. These URLs never change.

---

## MCP server

Prefer the remote OAuth server at `https://derive.to/mcp` (or `<instance>/mcp`). The local
compatibility server is `npx -y @derive-to/mcp` and shares the machine's `derive login`.

### Tools

The remote `/mcp` server has the complete ten-tool surface.

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `find` | Browse or search artifacts and discover askable workspace contexts |
| `read` | Read an artifact's content by short id; bundles take a `section` (page path), any read takes a `version` for history |
| `catch_up` | Read an artifact's review/change state, or the registered agent's queued work when called without a short id |
| `comment` | Leave feedback, reply (`reply_to` a thread id), anchor to a `quote`, and/or resolve/reopen (`set_state`) |
| `stage` | Upload large documents or bundles out of band; for an image/font, mint an asset upload URL, POST raw bytes, then use the returned permanent URL or bundle ref in `publish` |
| `publish` | Create or revise with `edits`, `content`, or `files`; `addresses` resolves threads and `request_review` opens a round |
| `organize` | Manage tags and collections |
| `checkpoint` | Save compact, resumable working state |
| `use` | Ask a workspace context or resume its session |
| `list_workspaces` | Inspect and route across granted workspaces |

The stdio compatibility server exposes `list_workspaces`, `list_artifacts`, `search`,
`read`, `catch_up`, `comment`, `organize`, and `publish`. It does not stage uploads,
query contexts, or checkpoint state.

### Resource

Remote: `derive://skills/publishing`, `/assets`, `/loop`, `/contexts`, `/checkpoint`, and `/organize`.
Stdio: `derive://guide`, `/guide/connect`, and `/guide/compatibility`.

### Claude Code project config

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "derive": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://derive.to/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

---

## Comment anchoring

Comments are anchored using W3C Web Annotation TextQuoteSelector: `{ exact, prefix, suffix }`.
The anchor client re-matches on each render using the exact text with surrounding context as
disambiguation. Anchors survive rewrites when the quoted text stays recognizable. When the
exact text is gone, the comment shows "text changed" rather than attaching to the wrong place.

---

## Deployment tiers

| Tier | Runtime | Metadata | Blobs | Realtime |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lite | Single container | SQLite | Local disk | In-process |
| Node Basic | Container(s) | Postgres | S3/R2 | In-process |
| Node Scale | Containers | Postgres | S3/R2 | Per-instance |
| Cloudflare Basic | Workers + DO | D1 | R2 | Durable Objects |
| Cloudflare Scale | Workers + DO | Postgres | R2 | Durable Objects |

### Lite (single container)

```bash
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml up -d
# opens at http://localhost:8080
```

### Node Basic

Set `DATABASE_URL` (Postgres) and `OBJECT_STORE_URL` (S3/R2). Container becomes stateless.

R2: `s3://<key>:<secret>@<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/<bucket>?region=auto`
S3: `s3://<key>:<secret>@s3.<region>.amazonaws.com/<bucket>?region=<region>`

### Node Scale

Run multiple stateless containers behind a load balancer for throughput. Realtime (SSE/presence)
stays on one instance and does not fan out across containers yet. Use a Cloudflare tier with
Durable Objects when you need cross-instance realtime. A shared Node backplane such as Redis is
planned but not built.

### Cloudflare Basic

```bash
cd apps/api
wrangler d1 create derive                                        # put database_id in wrangler.toml
wrangler d1 execute derive --remote --file=../../deploy/d1-schema.sql
pnpm exec tsx gen-auth-schema.ts > /tmp/auth-schema.sql
wrangler d1 execute derive --remote --file=/tmp/auth-schema.sql
wrangler r2 bucket create derive-blobs
pnpm build:web && wrangler deploy
wrangler secret put DERIVE_AUTH_SECRET
```

### Cloudflare Scale

Same as Cloudflare Basic but with `wrangler secret put DATABASE_URL` (Postgres). The Worker uses Postgres instead of D1; Durable Objects stay on the edge.

---

## Environment variables

| Var | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `BASE_URL` | request origin | Public URL for cookies and share links |
| `DERIVE_AUTH_SECRET` | generated | Session signing key; always set it in production |
| `PORT` | 8080 | Listen port (Node) |
| `DATA_DIR` | /data | SQLite + blob dir (Lite) |
| `DATABASE_URL` | (SQLite) | Postgres connection |
| `OBJECT_STORE_URL` | (local disk) | S3/R2 blob URL || `DERIVE_WEB_ORIGIN` | (none) | SPA origin for CORS (split CDN deploy) |
| `DERIVE_CROSS_SITE` | false | SameSite=None cookies for cross-origin SPA |
| `DERIVE_TOKEN` | (none) | Static bearer for CI/agents |
| `DERIVE_WEB_DIR` | (auto) | Override bundled SPA path |
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` / `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` | (none) | Google sign-in |
| `OIDC_ISSUER` / `OIDC_CLIENT_ID` / `OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` / `OIDC_PROVIDER_ID` | (none) | Enterprise SSO |

---

## Health endpoints

```
GET /healthz  -> 200 { ok: true }
GET /readyz   -> 200 { ok: true }
```

---

## Getting a DERIVE_TOKEN for direct API calls

Settings > Agents > New Agent. Name it, copy the `dk_agt_...` token (shown once).
Use as `Authorization: Bearer $DERIVE_TOKEN` in direct API requests. Remote MCP clients
should use OAuth instead of a pasted static token.
